nodeData.topic: Day 01 · The Only Shelter and Gopashtami
nodeData.note: SB 4.8.81, 2.10.1, 11.5.41, 10.15.1, 1.8.40; Bg 3.11 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. Maharaj explains how Dhruva Maharaj's mastery of prana chokes the breathing of the whole universe, and why the demigods run to Krishna as the only shelter who depends on no one, while everyone else is caught in a web of interdependence. Asked to speak on Gopashtami, he shows that Krishna maintains the world through the cow, tells how Krishna first went out to tend the cows and how the cows turned Vrindavan into soft dust for His feet, and calls devotees to become devotees of the cow. In the questions he answers vegans who reject milk, and suggests practical ways city devotees can serve mother cow. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj takes up the fourth canto, where Dhruva Maharaj's austerities have become so severe that he stops breathing. We live because the life air, prana vayu, is in the body; when it leaves, that is death.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:50 (auto-transcript): “So we are studying from the Bhagavatam, fourth canto where Dhruv Maharaj is doing Tapasya We know how Dhruva Maharaj is performing such severe austerities. He is performing such severe austerities that is so much so that he has stopped even breathing air. Now we are…”

Prana is not the soul but the link between consciousness, the subtle body and the gross body, and it is connected to the universal prana. Because Dhruva controls his own prana completely, he controls the cosmic prana too; for us, Maharaj says, imbalance of prana shows up as disease. — “Prana vayu is a very interesting thing. It is actually not the soul.”

🎙 Maharaj at 08:46 (auto-transcript): “Prana vayu is a very interesting thing. It is actually not the soul. It is actually the soul's connection and the consciousness connection with the subtle body. The subtle body's connection with the grass body is called prana and this prana is connected to the universal…”

In India we say a dying man's prana is over; nobody says his vitamins or protein have gone. Maharaj calls nutrients a gross science and says the body and the cosmos mirror each other, so knowing the body's prana opens the subtle science of the Vedas. — “The real science of the body is to know what is his prana.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:28 (auto-transcript): “When somebody dies traditionally in India, we say in Hindi, Prananthogaya, means his pranas existence in this body is over now. Nobody says Vitaminanthogaya, nobody says proteinanthogaya, He died because protein left, no, no, no, not because vitamin left. Protein, vitamin,…”

When Dhruva stops breathing nobody can breathe, and the suffocating demigods come to Krishna. Maharaj points out their good side, that in trouble they remember only Krishna, and their weakness, that they remember Him only in trouble. — “They remember only Krishna when they are in trouble.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:04 (auto-transcript): “He had total control over the entire cosmos to such an extent, when Dhruvamara stopped breathing, then nobody could breathe and all the devatas became suffocated. So whenever the devatas are in problem, what they do? They come and take shelter of Krishna. So there is one good…”

Krishna still loves the demigods, since He needs them to show the glory of His pure devotees. In the recent Govardhan pastime He shows the whole world that the Vrajavasis stand far above Indra and the other demigods. In the sixth canto Indra wins and Vritrasura is killed, yet Vritrasura is the one glorified: Krishna knows how to deal with every kind of devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:11 (auto-transcript): “Krishna somehow loves them. They see Krishna sees them that without the devatas I cannot do any pastime. Because until the devatas are there he cannot do any pastime. Because to glorify his devotees you require devatas. Like recently we had Gordhan Leela. The Gordhan pastime,…”

The demigods tell the Lord that all moving and non-moving beings are choking, that they do not know why, and that they have come to Him as the shelter of all for rescue. Maharaj notes that this time they do not even understand the cause, so they cannot first try their own strength.

Imagine suddenly being unable to breathe without knowing why. Other problems can wait; this one cannot, so the demigods rush to Krishna like patients in an ambulance. — “Breathing problem is the biggest emergency.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:06 (auto-transcript): “We don't know. Just imagine all of a sudden you are not able to breathe. What will happen? You don't know what is the cause. Like you run to a doctor when there is a problem, emergency. They all came in an emergency. Breathing problem is the biggest emergency. Some other…”

Krishna is called sharanam sharanyam, the one truly worthy of shelter, so to prove it He must act at once. Maharaj contrasts the time the demigods, with Brahma and Mother Earth, approached Him and He said He would come later; here they say waiting means everyone dies.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:22 (auto-transcript): “Now who are they? Who are you? You are Sharanam, Sharanyam. You are the ultimate shelter for everyone. So if you have to prove yourself to be the shelter of everyone, now you have to take immediate action now. Because if you say I will come later, in Krishna's past time what…”

Maharaj distinguishes the wind god of this world from the Vayu of Vaikuntha, presiding over the life airs, who appears as Hanuman, Bhima and Madhvacharya. Even Vayu cannot fix this, because the problem is not a lack of air; villagers grasp prana easily, he says, while a modern mechanistic education makes it bewildering.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:35 (auto-transcript): “You may think, why you did not go somewhere else? Why don't you go to Vayudeva? Because Vayu is the person who is in charge of the airs. Now we should know there are two Vayus. Vayudeva, the wind God. The wind God of the material world is different from the wind God of the…”

Of the Bhagavatam's ten subjects the last, ashraya, the shelter, is Krishna, and He is described as sva-ashraya-ashraya: His own shelter. Everyone we lean on in this world is leaning on someone else.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:01 (auto-transcript): “Now coming back to the point here, Krishna is addressed as Sharanam Sharanyam. If you want to know the name of Krishna mentioned in Bhagavatam, regarding the ten subject matters of Bhagavatam. Bhagavan Sva Ashraya Ashraya. Who is the Bhagavan? Now we know the ten subject…”

The tenth chapter of the second canto lists the ten subjects of the Bhagavatam and then says the first nine exist only to reveal the tenth, Krishna. Maharaj calls it a very interesting chapter to study.

Suta Goswami explains the shelter through adhyatma, adhibhuta and adhideva. A teacher needs students and a subject, a shop needs a seller, a buyer and goods, and the eye needs both an object and the sun; Krishna created this interdependence and alone stands outside it. — “it is the illusion to think that I am independent”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:53 (auto-transcript): “So that is why this is called interdependent system. Nobody can say in this world that I am independent. independent oh I have my money oh I got my job I have children I am independent no way the independence is the last thing which Krishna gives you you are completely…”

Maharaj speaks from India to listeners in America: a visa decision in Washington shakes thousands of Indian families, and an Indian tax change ripples back into the American economy. We cannot step out of this web unless we take full shelter of Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:18 (auto-transcript): “And that is what happens here. Now for example, I am sitting in India here. Now, you are all in America. Trump takes some decision. What happens? There are lots of families, thousands of families in India are affected. Some H1B visa, he does something with that. And here lots…”

Until we surrender we owe something to sages, other beings, relatives, ancestors and kings, from the nurse who served us at birth to the rulers who arranged our life. One who depends fully on Krishna owes nothing else, and Maharaj says even a five-year-old Dhruva shaking the cosmos teaches that every problem pushes us toward surrender. — “take shelter of Krishna, surrender to Krishna”

children.topic: Krishna maintains the world by cows
children.note:
Asked to speak on Gopashtami as well, Maharaj connects it to the verse: the shelter of all maintains the world, and He does it through the cow. That is why He is praised as the well-wisher of cows and brahmanas.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:18 (auto-transcript): “this. Now Krishna since I was also asked to speak something on Gopasthami. I don't know when are you celebrating Gopasthami. Yesterday we celebrated Gopasthami here in India. Now maybe you also must have celebrated Gopasthami yesterday. I don't know if it is today. But…”

Milk becomes yogurt, yogurt is churned into ghee, ghee is offered in sacrifice and eaten to give a brain fit for the Vedas. The brahmanas depend on the cow and the world depends on their sacrifice.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:28 (auto-transcript): “He maintains the world through the cows. You may be shocked! How does he maintain the world through the cows? He maintains the world through the cows. How? By cows you get the milk. When you get the milk, you boil the milk and make it into dahi, yogurt and then from the…”
Maharaj cites the Gita verse in which humans and demigods, through sacrifice, nourish one another. Krishna built this interdependence, and the cow sits at its root.

The cow is not worshipped from sentiment; of the seven mothers in scripture she is the chief, since our own mother fed only us while the cow feeds everyone. Brahminical culture rests on her, so demons attack the cow first, then the brahmanas, and society falls.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:07 (auto-transcript): “That is why cow is not just worship out of sentiment. It is actually not just an animal, it is a mother. We have seven kinds of mothers that is described in the Bhagavatam. But among all the seven kinds of mothers, the most important mother is the cow. Because cow is mother…”

children.topic: No Krishna bhakti without the cow
children.note:
Krishna and the cows cannot be separated: cow protectors without Krishna will fail, and chanters who ignore the cow miss something too. A man tells Maharaj he has chanted for twenty years without being happy; Maharaj asks what he has done for the cow. — “We cannot be Krishna Bhakta without becoming Go Bhakta”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:32 (auto-transcript): “Actually, if you want to really become Krishna Bhakta, we just cannot be Krishna Bhakta We cannot be Krishna Bhakta without becoming Go Bhakta Krishna and cows cannot be separated from each other. If you have Krishna they should be cow, if you have cows they should be…”

Krishna first tends the calves, and from then on He longs to tend the cows. Gopashtami is the day He finally goes out with them.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:31 (auto-transcript): “So that is what Krishna shows on the day of bhagupassami. He is just eagerly waiting. First actually Krishna, he became a Vatsapa. Vatsapa means one who takes care of the vatsas. Vatsapa means the calves. Now from that time onwards, he was constantly thinking that somehow or…”

For a year Krishna glances at Nanda Maharaj and turns away, and the anxious father asks his brothers why. They explain that Krishna sees him going out every day and wants to show He is grown up and can take over, like a teenage son sure he can run his father's business better.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:58 (auto-transcript): “And for past one year, somehow Krishna doesn't talk to Nanda Maharaj. Nanda Maharaj was always in anxiety. Why my son is not talking to him? Here Nanda Maharaj goes to Krishna and embraces him. Krishna looks at him a little bit with a small glance he gives. And he turns his…”

Nanda fears the Yamuna and Yashoda is unwilling until Balarama promises to look after Krishna. On the day the cows, trees and gopis wait eagerly, and only the parents find it hard; Maharaj says every parent has to digest the child becoming independent.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:53 (auto-transcript): “and all the Gopis in the Gopas in Vatsalvastha, it was not a good day for them Gopas. But somehow or other, now hard things have to be digested when the children grow up. The parents have to digest hard things, isn't it? There are so many things which the parents only know…”

With tilaka from Yashoda and friends around Him, Krishna calls and the cows follow. Maharaj calls the day a turning point: cowherding is a pretext to meet the gopis, and these purva-raga pastimes run from Gopashtami to Govardhan.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:36 (auto-transcript): “behind Krishna. Now, whole Gopasma-dila is actually a turning point, that is where Madhuriya-rasa, the beginning part, the Puragha, past times of Krishna started. The whole purpose of Krishna, going and tending the cows, is for what? It is nothing. He is only wanting just…”

The verse opening chapter fifteen of the tenth canto tells how Krishna and Balarama, now old enough to herd cows, make Vrindavan even more sacred with their footprints. Maharaj describes the Vrajavasis preserving and worshipping the marks of His soles in the dust.
Maharaj recalls Queen Kunti telling Krishna that the land prospers only because it bears the marks of His lotus feet.

children.topic: Cows grind the stones to dust
children.note:
Krishna refuses shoes unless all nine lakh cows get shoes too. Unable to bear stones and thorns under His feet, the cows break loose and pound the whole forest into soft dust overnight, an account Maharaj gives from the acharyas.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:17 (auto-transcript): “Now, soft dust of Vrindavan, actually how it came up, wonderful story is described by our Acharyas, where Krishna when he was allowed by some other, by Yeshoda and Nanda Maharaj to take care of the cows, a day before Bhopasthami, Krishna told that ok, tomorrow I am going to…”

Krishna hides His mercy in Vrindavan's dust, in Jagannath Puri's mahaprasad and in Navadvipa's holy name. So after hearing katha in Vrindavan, do not brush the dust off your clothes; it is His mercy, and the cows made it. — “Krishna has hidden his mercy in the dust of Vrindavan.”

🎙 Maharaj at 48:27 (auto-transcript): “And where did Krishna keep the mercy hidden? In Vrindavan, Krishna has hidden his mercy in the dust of Vrindavan. In Jagannathpuri, Krishna has hidden his mercy in the Mahaprasad. In Navadip, Krishna has hidden his mercy in the Holy Name. So if you have to go to Vrindavan, if…”

Krishna maintains the world through many things, but the cow carries it, and Maharaj notes how often Srila Prabhupada mentions her. Real prosperity rests on cow and land, not on notes or virtual money, and pure food depends on milk, the plowing bull and cow-dung manure.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:41 (auto-transcript): “Of course, how? Some people think, how is it so that Krishna maintains the entire world of the cows? No, Krishna maintains through so many things. Though there are so many things, it is the cow which maintains. Actually, all the demigods are there in mother cow. If you go and…”

By cow Maharaj means the native breeds found all over the world, not crossbred ones. A South American farmer tells him of the horned red cows of his childhood that foreign influence has pushed out.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:18 (auto-transcript): “I don't know, there's so much to be spoken about the cows, but when you say cow, what it means? It means actually the cows which are not genetically modified. Throughout the world, they were indigenous cows. Those are the cows which Krishna likes. What happened because of the…”

In South Indian temples following Pancaratra, the first sight shown to the Lord at mangala-arati is the back of a cow, where Lakshmi resides. Seeing that auspiciousness, the Lord spreads it to the whole world; Maharaj then closes and invites questions.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:37 (auto-transcript): “That is why Krishna, what is the first thing he sees? He sees the back part of the cow. If you go to South India temples, we also supposed to do that because we also follow Pancharatra but we don't have cows in our temple, that is why we don't do that. Every day in the…”

children.topic: Questions: vegans and serving the cow
children.note:
Listeners on the call in America ask how to answer vegans, how city people can serve the cow, about tooth powder, and where to begin in a meat-eating culture.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:07 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Prabhuji, Dhanod Pranama, Dr. Srila Prabhupada and Guru Maharaj. Very, very wonderful class Prabhuji and very nice explanation about the cows. Prabhuji, in America, we recently had a festival, it's called Vege Festival. and we met lots of Americans they are…”

At a vegetarian festival a devotee met kind people who condemn milk because the dairy industry also feeds slaughter. Maharaj says he met vegans in South America and first told them: you love animals, but we do not see the cow as an animal; she is our mother.

🎙 Question from the floor at 55:47 (auto-transcript): “and we met lots of Americans they are having so much compassion towards animal and they they don't eat meat and they advertise like why we should not eat meat and you know they sometimes some stalls they were showing the video how the animals are getting killed, some stalls…”

A scholar in King Krishnadevaraya's court asks which animal's milk is best; everyone says the cow's, but Tenali Rama says the goat's. His point: the cow is a mother, not an animal, so her milk does not count, and we do not drink a pig's or a tiger's milk either. — “Cow's milk is not animal milk because cow is not animal.”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:43 (auto-transcript): “Okay, so first thing is that we had to tell them, I told the story of Kanali Rama. Once, one scholar came to the court of Krishadevaraya and then he was a viking in South India, Krishadevaraya, Vaishnava. And then he told and asked entire sabadev, pundits there, which…”

Refusing milk so that cows are no longer bred is like sterilising all dogs so no dog is ever killed. Maharaj calls it false logic that would wipe out the species; the real problem is the idea of breeding animals for slaughter.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:29 (auto-transcript): “So their argument is so foolish. It is the saying that dogs are being killed. So don't produce the dog only. You just you artificial you make the infertility to all the dogs and no dogs, no killing. So then they got this point stuck. The very purpose what they say you should…”

children.topic: A cow is more than milk
children.note:
Slaughter happens because people value a cow only for milk. When dung and urine become fertiliser and medicine, a farmer keeps earning after she stops milking and has no reason to sell her; Maharaj knows well-run goshalas in profit and farmers who no longer sell cows.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:52 (auto-transcript): “I told, the concept is that when you take milk, naturally the farmer feels that I need to have more cows, I need to protect the cows. And when the cows stop giving milk, you still take the, protect the cow by taking the gober, that is the cow dung. From the cow dung you use…”

children.topic: Q2 · How to serve the cow?
children.note:
We express devotion to the cow as to our own mother. Maharaj grew up with cows in a village and admits this is hard to grasp in a city, so he gives practical steps.

🎙 Question from the floor at 65:37 (auto-transcript): “I did have a question and I don't know if you covered it when I missed it, missed the call. So you said we have to become a devotee of Krishna, we have to become a devotee of the cow. So how do we express devotion to the cow? Very good, very nice question. When we express our…”

Use bathing powder of mud and cow dung, tooth powder made from burnt dung, and desi cow ghee, and buy, sell and promote such products. A farmer who earns from them does not sell his cow to the slaughterhouse; in a village one can also feed and care for cows directly.

🎙 Maharaj at 66:36 (auto-transcript): “and now being in the city and never been with the cows how do you express our expectation practically what we can do at present is start using the cow products like we use soap it has got cow fat in it 100% animal fat is there in it now we are producing angarag angarag means…”

children.topic: Pickle from mother in the hostel
children.note:
In the hostel a little bottle of pickle from home is guarded like gold because it brings mother's presence. Living far from mother cow in a city, we feel her touch in the same way through her products.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:21 (auto-transcript): “So, like when we are in hostel, you are craving for mother's food. When you are in hostel, one small bottle of achar, we used to preserve it like more precious than gold. Even one small bit was enough because we used to feel the presence of mother in the form of achar, in the…”

children.topic: Q3 · What is in tooth powder?
children.note:
After a call drop Maharaj explains: burnt cow-dung cake becomes charcoal that removes odour, mixed with edible camphor, clove and herbs. Use the finger to massage the gums rather than brush the teeth, which, he says, Ayurveda teaches strengthens the teeth; he offers to send packets.

🎙 Question from the floor at 71:57 (auto-transcript): “follow-up question so you said yeah you get tooth powder is that made of cow Oh, my mouth has become very fresh. By putting fragrance from outside, that is not going to make our mouth fresh.”

A mother is shaken by Thanksgiving magazines full of meat and asks where to start in such a culture. Maharaj says to practise first, then speak: health opens doors that spirituality cannot, and he has seen several families become Krishna conscious through cow care; the movement has already begun.

🎙 Question from the floor at 82:27 (auto-transcript): “Lalitangi Mataji, you had one, some questions, right? Hare Krishna, Prabhupada. Thank you so much, Prabhupada. Very nice class. Prabhupada, we are a handful of people talking about the cows and how we worshipped the cows and the other day I had gone out to the doctor's office…”

nodeData.topic: Day 03 · The mirror: one yet different
nodeData.note: SB 4.28.63, 4.28.62 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. In the Puranjana story the Lord, appearing as a brahmana, tells His friend 'you and I are not different', and Maharaj explains why such verses are left open to misreading: the Lord satisfies even the desire to be God, and only the acaryas' commentaries keep us from being deluded. He walks through the three Mayavada theories (fragmentation, reflection and illusion) and Madhvacharya's answers: the illusion lies in our perception, the world is real, and the mirror image shows the soul's total dependence on the Lord. The class ends with Madhvacharya's coconut before King Jayasimha and questions on the Supersoul and on why Krishna bewilders. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj says he was invited to speak on management from the Bhagavatam later that day, but the class is his comfort zone. The context is still the story of Puranjana, an allegory told indirectly.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:30 (auto-transcript): “So, a month back or so, I received a letter from the GBC College to take a session on management principles based on Srimad Bhagavatam. I don't know what ghost entered into me to say yes to that. Actually, the one thing which I wanted to do was visit Pune, Kid Association of…”

At the end of the chapter Narada says the Lord is fond of what is said indirectly, because it increases rasa. Saying 'I love you' straight out has little effect; Maharaj notes that in village culture visitors talk of everything except their purpose, while the West wants it to the point. Even to ask for a loan, one first asks about the family. — “Krishna never tells anything direct”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:17 (auto-transcript): “is Puranjana Upakhyana. Last time we discussed about what is Upakhyana. What is the purpose of Upakhyana? Description of something which indirectly is a very interesting thing, not only for the who are hearing, not only for the speaker, but also for Krishna. Because at the…”

children.topic: The Lord appears as a brahmana
children.note:
Puranjana, now born as a woman, is grieving in separation after Malayadhvaja leaves his body. Maharaj says it is this separation that compels the Lord to appear before the devotee, now as a brahmana who speaks about the pure nature of the soul.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:13 (auto-transcript): “Now Krishna appeared as a Brahmin why he appeared because of the affection which the devotee has for the spiritual master of course all the analogies i will not get into because the topic is very serious here or very very very very deep here so the separation which the living…”

Maharaj calls verses 62 and 63 'deluding'. Like Mohini, who looks one way to the demons and another to the devotees, some passages of the Bhagavatam give one meaning to those who want to be God and another to devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:10 (auto-transcript): “While speaking about the pure nature of the soul, especially the 62 and 63, two verses, I don't know, these two numbers are always deluding, in the second chapter these two verses are always very deluding, 62 and 63. So these two verses are very deluding. Like Mohini deludes…”

Everybody wants to be a manager, an Isvara. The real controller is Krishna, so the controlling mentality ends in the claim 'I am also God'.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:05 (auto-transcript): “want to become a manager everybody has this tendency that i i want to control the controlling mentality is there so actually the controlling mentality controlling who is actual controller krishna so the controlling mentality means accepting that i am god i am also god…”

A child asked why he wants something gives a reason for it. In the same way every philosophy, Eastern or Western, only justifies a desire arising in conditioned consciousness, and Mayavada justifies 'I am the controller, I am the enjoyer'. — “So you require a philosophy to support your desire, isn't it?”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:34 (auto-transcript): “So you require a philosophy to support your desire, isn't it? Suppose a child is asking for something, then the parents say, why? He gives a philosophy for it. Actually all the philosophies are actually supporting a particular kind of desire which raises in the conditioned…”

The verse calls the Lord the one who satisfies everyone's desires. Some souls want to be convinced they are God, so the Lord leaves room for that philosophy; Maharaj says the Upanishads especially leave scope for misreading, the Bhagavatam far less, yet still some.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:26 (auto-transcript): “And the last line it is said, means the Lord is one who satisfies the desires of every living entity. And there are quite a number of living entities who want to be convinced that I am God. So Krishna has to give a philosophy to satisfy the desire. It is the nature of the…”

The previous verse, in which the brahmana tells his friend that they are not two different persons, reads on its face like complete oneness of soul and God. Maharaj goes through its words to show how strongly it can be taken that way.

First, to delude those who want to become God. Second, to know the right philosophy one must know the wrong one, which is why commentaries exist; without them it is very hard to ascertain the truth.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:26 (auto-transcript): “So in this way, you should see yourself as me, you as me. In this way, it's total Jiveshwaravada. So now, the question comes that why is it spoken here, in this context here, because one is delude, delusion, to delude the conditioned souls, to delude those people who are…”

In Srila Prabhupada's time someone suggested that printing only the verse and translation of the Hindi Gita would sell thousands more. When the idea was brought to him, Prabhupada answered angrily that without his purports it was better not to distribute Gitas at all. — “so that shows that the commentary”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:13 (auto-transcript): “Once, His Holiness Srila Gopalakish Goswami Maharaj, at that time it was not His Holiness, Prabhupada's time, it was Kumbhavindashvila Prabhupada was also there and at that time book distribution was going on, Hindi Bhagavad Gita was being sold, newly published and being…”

This verse uses the image of seeing oneself reflected to show both oneness and difference between the living entity and the Lord. Maharaj explains that one can see oneself in a mirror and also in another person's eye.

Two images exist, but they are not alike: the one in the mirror is clear and bright, the one in the eyeball is dim. The difference is plain to see.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:18 (auto-transcript): “What is the difference? One is very bright Another one is very dim The reflection is very dim Of course taking the same example Srila Prabhupada gives in a different way He takes the sun The sun is reflected in the pot of water That is also sun And the sun is also sun But the…”

Srila Prabhupada gives the same point with the sun reflected in a pot of water. Both are called sun, but the reflection can never claim to be as powerful as the sun itself.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:28 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupada gives in a different way He takes the sun The sun is reflected in the pot of water That is also sun And the sun is also sun But the reflection cannot claim That I am as good as the sun As powerful as the sun In this way distinction is established Now even…”

Even from this verse a Mayavadi reading can be drawn. Maharaj summarises their view: one undifferentiated Brahman becomes covered by maya, whose knowledge potency makes Isvara (even Krishna's body, they say, is matter) and whose ignorance potency makes the living entities.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:51 (auto-transcript): “There is a scope of deriving Mayavada philosophy from that. There is a section in the Mayavada philosophy called Pratibhimbavada. Because Pratibhimbavada is spoken in the Vedas also. What is the meaning of Pratibhimbavada? Pratibhimbavada means the theory of reflection. They…”

They are called Mayavadis because they hold that Isvara, the Lord Himself, is a product of maya. They accept a difference between Isvara and the jiva, but say both arise from Brahman's contact with maya.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:23 (auto-transcript): “That is why they are called Mayavadis Mayavadis are called Mayavadis because they say Ishvara is a product of Maya When Brahman is affected by the Vidya potency And they say this Vidya potency Because Brahman is affected by Vidya potency Body of Krishna is made of matter But…”

Before joining, Maharaj explained these ideas at a Ramakrishna Math in Mysore, and a sannyasi there said he spoke their philosophy better than they did. Maharaj credits Caitanya Mahaprabhu's talks with Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya and Prakasananda Sarasvati, and urges devotees to study them. — “We are very clear about their philosophy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:01 (auto-transcript): “When I spoke these things in one place, before I joined this, I spoke these things in one R.K. Madhra, Ramakrishna Madhra in Mysore. So I was speaking to one sanyasi. He told, oh, you are speaking your philosophy so nicely and better than us. So I don't speak to give a class…”

If Brahman cannot be cut, how did it break into many small souls? Unable to answer, they moved from the theory of fragmentation (pariccheda-vada) to that of reflection (pratibimba-vada): Brahman is not divided, only reflected on maya, like the sun on many waves.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:09 (auto-transcript): “is how did this whole big brahman which you say undifferentiated brahman become small small fragmented parts like your living entities so because brahman is akhandaniya it cannot be khandaram it cannot be uh cleavable it is not cleavable she'll probably use the word cleavable…”

To cover one lie you must tell another, so Mayavada keeps expanding and has hundreds of varieties, though it says there is no variety. Truth is one, like the one Hare Krishna maha-mantra. — “Truth is always one”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:01 (auto-transcript): “To cover one lie you have to tell another lie To cover that lie you have to tell another lie In this way one lie leads to Hundreds of lies So Mayavad is actually nothing but Expansion and expansion of lies It is not this one kind of Mayavad There are hundreds and hundreds…”

A reflection needs a surface. If Brahman is all-pervading and reflects in itself, then part of Brahman is maya and part is pure, and nobody can explain which is which.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:40 (auto-transcript): “Of course there are many problems, but a major problem is, if you say Brahman is all-pervading, where is it reflected? For something to reflect, you have to have a substratum of reflection. Is Brahman getting reflected into itself? If Brahman is getting reflected into itself,…”

So a third theory came, vivarta, the theory of illusion, which Sankaracarya built his whole system on. Maharaj then shows how Madhvacharya turns its own example against it.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:23 (auto-transcript): “Neither Parichedavad, neither Pratimavad. We will talk to you something, it is Vivarta. Third thing came, Vivarta. What is Vivarta? Vivarta means theory of illusion, theory of fragmentation, parichetvād, theory of reflection, that is called pratibambhuvād, and the third one…”

Walking in the dark, one takes a rope for a snake; in the same way, they say, we see a world that is not really there.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:00 (auto-transcript): “Like you are walking on the road And you find there is a Robe But because it is dark Because you are in ignorance You think that rope to be the snake That is called vivarta Illusion, theory of illusion Now Sri Padma Dvacharya He is Acharya who actually Destroyed the Mayava…”

Maharaj recalls Srila Prabhupada writing in a Caitanya-caritamrita purport that Madhvacharya and Ramanujacarya defeated the so-called Vedantists; Madhva in particular demolished the idea that the soul and God are identical.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:14 (auto-transcript): “Now Sri Padma Dvacharya He is Acharya who actually Destroyed the Mayava philosophy completely Srila Prabhupada One of the purports in Chaitanya Chiritamrita He says that Sri Padma Dvacharya and Shri Pada Ramanujacharya, both of them kicked on the face of the Vedantis and made…”

children.topic: The illusion is in the seer
children.note:
Madhva asks where the illusion is. A real snake must exist somewhere for the mistake to occur, and the rope in front is real too; the fault lies only in the perception of the person looking. — “The problem is with the perception”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:13 (auto-transcript): “So now he takes his philosophy and then says, okay, a man is walking in the road, it's dark. And he saw the road to be the snake which is not there. In the same way, we are in darkness, so we are seeing the Maya, we are seeing the world, but it is actually not there. Then…”

So Madhva establishes that the world is real, temporary but true, because it is Krishna's energy, and the living entities are real too, not false appearances.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:48 (auto-transcript): “So Shri Padma Bhavacharya establishes this principle called Jagat Satyam Brahma Satyam Jagat Pitya No This world is truth Jagat is satya, it is truth It may be temporary, but it is truth It is because it is energy of Krishna In this way, he establishes the world The living…”

Madhvacharya also saw reflection described in the Vedas and explained it properly as bimba-pratibimba, original and image: a picture of the soul's complete dependence on the Lord.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:24 (auto-transcript): “The philosophy Of reflection Hiroshripa Shankar Madhvacharya, who actually, he perceived the Vedas, which talk about vivartai, talks about illusion, and explain what actual illusion is. He saw in the Vedas, there is a description of Pratibimba, like reflection is being…”

The person in the mirror can lift his hand only when the real person lifts his. In the same way the living entity can act only when the Lord sanctions it. — “When I am speaking, who is speaking? Krishna is speaking.”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:46 (auto-transcript): “of the mirror. The person in the mirror, when can he lift the hand? When the real person lift? In the same way, a living entity can lift the hand only when the Supreme Lord sanctions it. So it is talking about surrender. It is not talking about the oneness. It is talking…”

So the example teaches surrender, not oneness. If there is oneness at all, it is oneness in the sense of dependence. — “It is talking about the surrender.”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:07 (auto-transcript): “about surrender. It is not talking about the oneness. It is talking about the surrender. Every activity we do, I am speaking because Krishna is speaking. I am lifting the hand because Krishna lifted the hand. Because the reflection can only do anything until less. Only when…”

Maharaj closes with an incident from Madhvacharya's first tour south, to Kumbla below Udupi in today's Kerala.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:02 (auto-transcript): “When Sri Padmanavachari was travelling to First tour, he was going to South India For him, South India means to go to South India. For him, South India means to go down below Udupi, it's called false name, to go to Kerala. So the first city which he came in Kerala is called…”

A rival Sankara-follower, thinking Madhva's strength came from his huge library, had thieves steal his books. Madhva's disciples complained to King Jayasimha, who understood at once, sent soldiers to recover the books and invited Madhva to his palace.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:27 (auto-transcript): “So there, Sripash Shankaracharya, not Adi Shankara, at that time who was Shankaracharya, he saw Madhavacharya is the greatest, the biggest library which anybody could have. He had manifest library and unmanifest libraries too He had vision for some scriptures Which were not…”

The king asks: scripture calls both the living entity and the Supreme Lord 'Brahman', so how can they be different? Maharaj marvels at the calibre of such kings.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:33 (auto-transcript): “then Jai Simha he asked Madhavacharya one question Just imagine what kind of caliber Those kind of kings had The question was In the scriptures The living entity is also called Brahman And the supreme lord is also called Brahman How are you saying both are different That was…”

Seeing that people's intelligence had become gross, Madhva asks for a dried coconut and shows each part: husk, shell, kernel. Together we call it all 'coconut', yet up close each is distinct; so everything is Brahman, but the soul, matter and the Lord remain distinct.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:03 (auto-transcript): “Then Madhavacharya told Bring a coconut because by the time Madhavacharya came he saw people's intelligence have become very gross until unless I give something very so called practical some slides or something like that it's very difficult for people to get things so he knew…”

Maharaj adds that our line explains this as inconceivable oneness and difference, and that Bhaktivinoda Thakura describes the souls as separated parts of the Lord. The fire and spark, and the sun and its particles, are examples found in both sruti and smrti.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:29 (auto-transcript): “So this is how Shri Padma Dvacharya He though Externally presented the philosophy Of Bhimpa Pratibha Vada or Dvaita But without Achintya Beda Beda Vinnamscha Jeevan Like Bhaktino Thakur actually Gives a very elaborate description Of this particular Vinnamscha Jeevan Vinnam…”

The same Bhagavatam gives nectar to devotees and cheats the demons, as Mohini did. Taking shelter of the spiritual master and the acaryas' commentaries makes one a demigod who receives the nectar; without it one may become a demon even while reading the Bhagavatam.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:30 (auto-transcript): “this in Bhagavatam which are deluding you will not be deluded. Ghatakash, vhatakash, even that verse is also there in the Bhagavatam. In the 12th Canto, you will find these verses which talks about this thing. So we should be very careful. Bhagavatam is deluding to demons…”

Maharaj invites questions; a comment and two questions follow before the announcements.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:36 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, thank you for a wonderful discourse and breaking it down. I really appreciate it. I was thinking of this particular, just a comment, I was thinking of this particular scenario, that of course there is a philosophical way to look at it as you broke it down piece…”

children.topic: Q1 · A father and his son
children.note:
A listener offers a devotional angle: like a father telling a drifting teenage son 'we are almost the same', the Lord's words may show His intimacy and ask the soul not to stray far. Maharaj's reply is not clearly recorded.

🎙 Question from the floor at 52:54 (auto-transcript): “I was thinking of this particular, just a comment, I was thinking of this particular scenario, that of course there is a philosophical way to look at it as you broke it down piece by piece. And then there is another angle, you can say a personal or devotional angle to look at…”
Asked whether each being has its own Paramatma, Maharaj says there is one: in a room of ten people there are ten souls but one Supersoul, undivided though He seems divided.

children.topic: All these 'vadas' are in the Veda
children.note:
Reflection, fragmentation and the other theories all appear in the Vedas; Mayavada did not create them. The problem is only misinterpretation, and each has a proper reading.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:04 (auto-transcript): “As we should be very clear, all these vads, whether it's Pratibhima vada, Pariched vada, Drishti-Shishti vada, so many kinds of vads, they are all in the Veda. It is not that there is a creation of Mayavada, it is a misinterpretation, which is a problem. And there is a proper…”

If the Bhagavatam rejects cheating religion out of compassion, why should it delude anyone? Maharaj answers that Krishna's very nature is to bewilder, devotees and demons alike, and the Bhagavatam is His form; some things are meant only for the qualified, and that qualification comes by the acaryas' mercy. — “very nature of Krishna is to delude.”

🎙 Question from the floor at 55:38 (auto-transcript): “The Bhagavatam, like the Dharma Projata Kaithav, so especially the kaitha dharma about the moksha like people taking to the impersonal path had to be rejected so in that as you are mentioning that it was to delude so the bhagatav is to bring out the ultimate but in that like…”

children.topic: The gopis who could not go
children.note: In the Tenth Canto some gopis are held back at home; their separation burns away 'sin' and their inner embrace of Krishna exhausts 'piety'. Since the gopis have neither, Maharaj gives Visvanatha Cakravarti's reading: before that pain and joy all the pains and pleasures of this world become insignificant.

Maharaj says Krishna even arranged the Devi Bhagavata with very similar descriptions, so that Jiva Goswami had to write to establish which is the real Bhagavatam. Delusion is always there.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:54 (auto-transcript): “Even want to speak of this The very Bhagavatam itself Krishna has arranged one book called Devi Bhagavat and there are a lot of descriptions which are exactly similar of both the scriptures so Jeeva Goswami Prabhupada has to write a book on establishing that this Bhagavatam…”
